card.architecture: Boogu-Image-0.1 10B unified DiT (Qwen3-VL encoder, FLUX.1 VAE); Apache-2.0; bf16 (full precision)
card.summary: Brand-new (0.1) Apache-2.0 text-to-image foundation model. 10B unified gen+edit family; the Base variant targets diversity, controllability, and dense bilingual text rendering (run at 2K for the densest text/poster layouts). Real CFG (~4). Runs bf16 on a 24 GB card (the fp8 encoder offloads before the diffusion model loads). The flow-matching shift (3.16) is applied automatically at load.
use_cases: dense / layout-heavy in-image text (posters, documents, bilingual designs)
a clean Apache-2.0 base for downstream development
card.pick_when: You want to try the new Boogu base model, or need dense/bilingual in-image text, on a 24 GB card.

prompt.guidance: Detailed natural-language prose (EN or ZH). Quote literal text to render it.
prompt.example: A vintage travel poster for the Alps at sunrise, bold headline reading "WANDER" in cream serif letters, snow peaks and a winding railway, textured paper grain
prompt.instructions: Write descriptive natural language (English or Chinese); specificity and word order matter. To render literal text, wrap the exact string in double quotes and keep it short. Recommended (model card): 25-50 steps (50 for best fidelity), CFG 2.0-5.0 (4.0 is a good default), euler/simple. Native ~1K; bump width/height to ~2K for the densest text/poster layouts. Negative prompts are supported (real CFG).
do: Quote literal on-image text and keep it short
Use a light negative if needed
dont: Expect long paragraphs of in-image text to stay perfect at 1K

speed.note: 10B bf16; the fp8 text encoder offloads before the diffusion model loads so it fits unquantized on 24 GB.
speed.measured_note: Not yet benchmarked on this box.

ui_help.note: Describe what you want in plain words. Strong here for images that need readable, dense, or bilingual text.
